    BONUS STAGE

    THE DATA BEHIND I'M BABY

    What tens of thousands of parent checklists, in 36 languages, say about how first words work.

    LOOK UP A WORD

    Pick a meaning to see when babies say it in each language, and what they actually say.

    WHERE THE WORDS COME FROM

    Parents filled in the MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories and their adaptations: checklists of several hundred words, marking which ones their child understands and says. Wordbank (Frank, Braginsky, Yurovsky & Marchman) archives over 100,000 of these forms and links words across languages by meaning. CC BY 4.0.

    WHEN A WORD IS COLLECTED

    Each word appears at the age when half of children say it, from a logistic curve fit to the share of children saying it at each month. "Heard, not said yet" uses the same method for understanding, which is only measured in younger toddlers. Each language's checklist has its own words, so compare languages loosely.

    ADULT FREQUENCY

    Adult word ranks come from 2018 OpenSubtitles counts (FrequencyWords). Only single words are matched; no list was available for Cantonese, Faroese or Japanese. Animals and vehicles in the world stand where their word is collected.

    THE DATA SECTION

    Cross-language figures use the 36 languages in the game. "Earliest" and "latest" words are meanings found in at least 20 languages; the bars span the middle half. The understanding gap uses words measured both ways in at least 10 languages.

    "Most and least typical" uses weighted log odds with an informative Dirichlet prior (Monroe, Colaresi & Quinn, 2008). For each language, the share of children saying each meaning is averaged over every month measured up to 48 months (the first four years; most checklists stop at 30 to 36 months) and scaled to the same total, so every language counts equally. Words a checklist only asks about on its infant form, up to about 18 months, are left out for that language. The comparison group is the other 35 languages, and the prior is one average language. Only meanings on at least 20 checklists are included.

    OTHER LANGUAGES

    Comparisons use the median age for the same meaning across Wordbank languages that have it (at least eight), after allowing for each checklist's overall pace. Sign languages and samples of mostly older children are left out.
